english.title: Import goods other than a controlled drug to which a prohibition / restriction applies for the time being
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were concerned in the importation of goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..) with intent to evade the prohibition or restriction on importation imposed by **(..SPECIFY LEGISLATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 50(3) and (4) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
improperly imported goods
to which a prohibition / restriction applied

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies after the 21/02/2024 following commencement of the Finance Act 2024, amending subsection 50(4) to increase the maximum penalty for conviction on indictment from 7 to 14 years. For offences applying after this date, see H102629.
(ii) This offence code should not be used for the importation of firearms (see H10654), drugs or counterfeit notes / currency (see H10655). This offence code is appropriate for the importation of offensive weapons (as listed in The Criminal Justice Act 1988 (Offensive Weapons Order) 1988.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or three times the value of the goods involved, whichever is the greater.
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions
20 years
